answer.rationale: Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so renew or negotiate cannot hit the 18% cut. The contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferral is not like the prior non-critical month-to-month case and would risk a gap at 94% utilization with no buffer. The low-cost quote meets the mandate; c2 says that vendor already ran as primary with quick onboarding, which is the only path that both secures supply past expiry and lowers TCO. That does not prove they can absorb this load in 14 days without starving the line—c1 is the counter-evidence that incumbent renewal was what kept deliveries and integration stable. Verifying c2 and c1 before treating last year as transferable. Delivery/downstream disruption risk is material; do not assume a clean broad cutover.
